I am 66 years old, finished middle school, and have been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. My family has 7 people. My son and daughter-in-law work at a factory in town, but they come back for harvest and busy times. We have a well for irrigation, so water is manageable.

I split my land into two parts. I put 9 mu into the wheat-maize rotation — that is my main field. The other 3 mu I keep for cotton. My wife wants the cotton because we use the cottonseed oil at home and the stalks are good for fuel.

For the winter wheat on the 9 mu: I will plant Jimai 22, an improved variety I have used for several years. The seed dealer always pushes new names, but my neighbor Lao Wang planted Jimai 22 last year and got over 500 kg per mu, so I trust it. I buy 50 kg bags of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer. Before planting, I spread one full bag per mu as basal fertilizer — that gives 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu. Then at the wheat jointing stage in March, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu, about 20 kg, which adds another 9 kg of nitrogen. So total I put about 16 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I never skip the jointing fertilizer — I tried saving money once in 2012 and the wheat turned yellow, the ears were small, and I lost a lot of money. Never again. I irrigate three times: overwintering water in November, jointing water in spring, and grain-filling water in May. I spray herbicide once after planting and fungicide once at heading stage, so two pesticide applications. I rotary till before sowing. Last year I got 530 kg per mu; this year if the frost is not too bad, I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the summer maize on the same 9 mu: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I hire a tractor with a rotary tiller to prepare the ground fast, then plant hybrid maize. I use Zhengdan 958, a hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. At planting I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 6 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium. When the plants reach the big trumpet leaf stage, I spread another 15 kg of urea per mu, about 7 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen is about 13 kg per mu. Summer maize gets rain from the July storms, so I only irrigate once if the drought is bad, usually at filling stage. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for corn borer, so two pesticide times. If the weather is normal, I expect 600 kg per mu.

For the 3 mu of cotton: Cotton is hard work, but I know how to do it. In April I deep plough the cotton field. I plant hybrid cotton, about 1.5 kg seed per mu. Cotton needs more potassium or the bolls don't open properly. I use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and later I add urea and extra potassium sulfate. Total per mu I put about 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium. I irrigate twice — once at flowering and once at boll stage. Pesticide is four times because aphids and bollworms always come, and if you are late by even a few days you lose the whole crop. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I think about costs every day. Last year a bag of urea was over 100 yuan. For 12 mu, fertilizer is thousands of yuan. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means no money for my grandson's school fees. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I watch my neighbors closely. If Lao Wang and Old Li put 50 kg compound per mu, I do the same. If they add more urea at jointing, I add more. Change is risky. I start from what I did last year and adjust a little, not from a blank slate.
